brief: GS midday color: US equities sell off (SPX -1.1%, with RTY underperforming NDX underperforming SPX) after a hot September core CPI print (33bps vs 20bps consensus, driven by shelter) pushed the 5y/10y/30y above 2007 highs. Bloomberg-implied Fed hike odds rose to 40% for October and 88% for December; GS's GIR still expects a second hike in December and is watching tomorrow's PPI report and Warsh's Bangkok speech for timing clarity. Rate-sensitive baskets underperform (Non-Profitable Tech -4.8%, HY Debt Sensitive -4.5%, Home Builders -2.5%) while a quality/safety bid emerges (Cyclicals vs Defensives -1.3%, Healthcare +2.2%). Neoclouds are pressured by social-media chatter about bond yields hitting 15%; semis (SOXX -3.9%) are on track for a sixth straight losing session. Bank earnings disappoint: BAC -5.9% on operational-flexibility scrutiny, MS -3.6% on a PT income/wealth miss, STT -6.3% on a servicing/FX-driven top-line miss. Volumes are elevated (ETF 33% of tape, exchanges +13% vs 20dma); GS's own franchise flow reads 6/10 activity and 8.9% skewed for sale, with LOs (19.5%) and HFs (12.6%) both net sellers. The desk's Chart of the Day argues decelerating AI/non-AI growth next year favors quality, backing a Defensives-over-Cyclicals, short-low-quality stance.
